title: Signal ownership matrix and dashboard culling brainstorm
content:
Context and goal:
This is a working brain-dump from the observability sync (2025-02-14). Goal: produce a lightweight, actionable ownership map for signals and a simple, repeatable dashboard culling heuristic we can use during quarterly telemetry reviews. Keep it pragmatic: low ceremony, fast decisions, clear escalation paths.

High-level constraints (reminder):
- Query cost and cardinality limits matter for inference telemetry (tokenized request traces can explode cardinality).
- Multi-tenant tagging and privacy (PII/PHI) must be preserved: default redaction at ingestion, allow scoped enrichment only for owners with approvals.
- Dashboards should serve two classes: operator (SRE/ops) and product/feature owners. Avoid mixing both on the same panel.

Signal ownership matrix (sketch):
- signal_name: operator_adopter: product_adopter: retention: criticality (note this is prose, convert to canonical spreadsheet later)
- request_latency_p50/p95/p99: eng-sre : product-hosted-api : 90d : high
- kv_cache_hit_ratio: eng-serving-runtime : eng-serving-runtime : 30d : medium
- token_cost_per_route: eng-costing : product-hosted-api : 180d : medium-high
- fallback_rate_per_model_variant: eng-platform-routing : eng-dedicated : 90d : high
- embedding-fanout-count: eng-observability : product-embed-api : 30d : low
- trace_sampled_span_count: eng-observability : eng-sre : 14d : high
Notes: owners are the team responsible for correct instrumentation, adopters are teams that rely on the signal for decisions/alerts.

Quick ownership rules (to convert to policy):
- If a signal impacts SLA or billing, priority = high and owner must be a platform/infra team.
- Product-level fidelity (per-customer) -> owner is product team, but collect aggregate by default.
- Any signal with > 1m unique tag keys per month triggers review and potential cardinality reduction.

Metric definition examples (canonical template inline):
- name: downstream_request_latency_ms
  definition: end-to-end request latency from API ingress to final token flush (exclude streaming buffering gaps)
  unit: milliseconds
  cardinality_tags: model_id, region, route
  collection_frequency: per-request (aggregated into quantiles)
  alert_thresholds: p99 > 1200ms for 10m -> paged

- name: kv_cache_miss_rate
  definition: fraction of token-attached requests that do not find warm KV cache entry for session prefix
  unit: ratio
  cardinality_tags: tenant_id (hashed), model_family
  collection_frequency: per-session update, aggregated per-minute
  alert_thresholds: sustained > 5% for 30m -> paging optional

Tracing annotation conventions (proposal):
- Every request should carry a root trace with these high-level tags: trace.kind=server, r.rt.gateway_ms, r.rt.kv_cache_ms, r.input_tokens, r.output_tokens, model_variant.
- Add span-level attributes for heavy ops: load_model_ms, quantize_ms, compile_kernel_ms, batch_wait_ms. Keep attr names short and snake_case.
- Privacy: redact prompt_text and any free-text user fields at ingestion. Instead add a deterministic prompt_hash for replay and eval correlation.
- Sampling: adaptive reservoir by tenant tier + error-first sampling. Target: 100 traces/min per region baseline; error spikes increase retention multiplier automatically.

Dashboard culling heuristic (weekly rubric):
- Step 0: owners present the dashboard and answer: who uses this? Why is it not covered elsewhere?
- Step 1: Age check: if a widget hasn't been viewed by a human in 60 days and has no active alert, mark for review.
- Step 2: Query cost: if the widget costs > $X/month (proxy by query bytes or execution time) and is low usage, propose archive.
- Step 3: Signal redundancy: if >2 widgets show same time-series across dashboards, consolidate into a single canonical panel and link others to it.
- Step 4: Cardinality risk: any panel that expands tags > 10k unique values in a 7d window is flagged for cardinality reduction or rollup.
- Step 5: SLI mapping: keep only panels that map to an SLO or a known operational runbook; everything else should be distilled into a monthly report.

Operator vs product dashboards (guideline):
- Operator dashboards: 1 row per failure mode, show impact (requests/min lost), top 3 correlated signals, and playbook link. Minimal long historical tails.
- Product dashboards: cohort-focused, include session-warmth and perceptual metrics (utility), allow deeper historical window but aggregated.

Rollout instrumentation checklist (pre-rollout):
- Add tracing hooks for all new control-plane calls (quick span anchor points)
- Ensure model_variant tag present on all request-level metrics
- Add synthetic probe that exercises the new route at percentiles representative of real traffic (small canary probes)
- Create one dashboard widget that surfaces the new metric and mark owner in dashboard metadata
- Add a regression alert to the staging alias environment first, then prod with a higher threshold

Draft alert prioritization flow (operational):
- page for severity S1 (customer-impacting + automated rollback race)
- notify on-call SRE channel for S2 (sustained SLO risk)
- create ticket and assign to owner for S3 (informational)

Low-friction instrumentation conventions (to adopt):
- default tag set: {env, region, tenant_hash, model_family, route}
- metric names use kebab or snake? go with snake_case for all infra metrics to match existing DSL
- avoid free-text keys in metric labels; use enums where possible

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs:
- What is the exact $X monthly query cost threshold? (Ops/finance sync needed)
- Should we enforce a telemetry schema at ingestion for new teams, or opt-in linting? (tradeoff: speed vs long-term hygiene)
- How aggressively do we downsample small-tenant traces by default? Current sim suggests 3x cost savings but weaker debugging for outliers.

Immediate next steps (owners assigned):
- Maya: convert signal sketch above to a spreadsheet and assign primary/secondary owners (due 2025-02-21)
- Priya: draft a short Confluence page with the dashboard culling rubric and email cadence for reviews (due 2025-02-28)
- Liam: prototype a trace-sampler that applies tenant-tier multipliers in the telemetry sandbox (PR linked above) (due 2025-03-07)
- Diego & Sofia: run a 1-week query-cost audit of top 50 dashboard panels and produce a cost/usage matrix (due 2025-03-10)

Notes to self: keep this doc short and actionable; don't try to re-invent the metric catalog here. We need guardrails and a decision loop.

Appendix (quick commands and links):
- Top query producers: run analytics query: "SELECT dashboard_id, sum(cost) FROM query_logs WHERE ts>now()-30d GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 50"
- Trace replay hint: use prompt_hash + trace_id to reconstruct sanitized replay in private sandbox

End of brainstorm.
